abstract: Design rung 1 for issue 87, manifest member identity, authored in worktree design-87 on branch design/member-identity-87 over base 51fb403 and committed at 9e18799ace9332d6d4b472bb2d46a77f1666bf5c as docs/design/2026-07-27-manifest-member-identity-design.md, 564 lines, single file, board untouched so no collision with the in-flight freight work, nothing pushed. Section 0 rules BOTH and keeps the format half out of prose on the strength of a landed prior verdict. The conductor's central premise - that a member's identity lives in one field serving two masters - was attacked and measured false: the pressure comes from a 10-line consumer function that reads exactly one member key, and that accident of code was promoted into a property of the format. Six probes ran against a board server built from source over sealed scratch stores, all landed in a new section 2b with a re-derivation recipe. The decisive one reframes the rejected shapes: shape B, measured against a real runtime-id dispatch instead of an empty store, renders a returned member as declared-not-observed with zero conditions, a Law 1 confident falsehood rather than the cosmetic placeholder cost the owner's ruling recorded, while shape A degrades to Law 4 silent loss - both correct only while a human remembers to amend. The design removes the amendment entirely: a member is named by the shop-minted task-id it already has, never by a runtime fact, and the plan-to-actual binding is derived by the assembler from data both sides already carry, with an explicit legacy clause proven necessary by measurement over the landed corpus and an ambiguity disclosure proven absent today. Three previously unstated premises were surfaced and attacked, one of which localises the whole shape A versus shape B disagreement to a single missing launch-time wire that 97 captured payloads show a dedicated field already available for. Two self-disclosures are on the record, including a write into the shared checkout that also rendered one fault injection vacuous, caught, cleaned, and redone under observation.
